title: Morning Cybersecurity Digest
subtitle: Friday, November 27 - Here's what's worth your attention today.

items.title: Drupal warns of new critical flaw exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-136716)
items.summary: Drupal has warned of a new highly critical flaw in Drupal Core, CVE-2026-136716, that attackers are actively exploiting to take over vulnerable websites where the installer remains remotely accessible.
items.details: The flaw relates to improper handling of unusual or incomplete installation states and follows the November 18 Fail2Install fix (CVE-2026-132165, SA-CORE-2026-017). Drupal confirmed exploitation in the wild and urged admins to check logs for unauthorised access and unexpected changes involving the main administrative account (user 1).
items.action: Update to Drupal 11.4.14, 11.3.23 or 10.6.23, run update.php, remove or block remote access to install.php, and review logs from November 19 onward for compromise.

items.title: SolarWinds Serv-U 2026.4 fixes nine critical flaws, two giving Linux root
items.summary: SolarWinds released Serv-U 2026.4 on November 24 fixing 18 vulnerabilities, including nine critical flaws; CVE-2026-123172 and CVE-2026-123168 could grant attackers root access on Linux servers.
items.details: Other critical flaws include CVE-2026-82322 (9.1, IDOR letting a domain group admin become a Serv-U server admin) and CVE-2026-82320 / CVE-2026-82321 (type confusion and privilege escalation). SolarWinds credited the Intigriti Bug Bounty Program for the critical reports and reported no active exploitation of the new flaws.
items.action: Upgrade internet-facing Serv-U servers, starting with Linux, to 2026.4 and review admin accounts and file-access logs.

items.title: VMware vCenter auth bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8) now has public PoC
items.summary: Rapid7 published a technical breakdown and Metasploit module for the actively exploited VMware vCenter authentication bypass CVE-2026-123890 (CVSS 9.8), and public proof-of-concept code is now live.
items.details: Broadcom shipped fixes in advisory VMSA-2026-0009 on November 19 after Mandiant warned of live attacks. Mandiant and Google Threat Intelligence tie exploitation to the China-nexus group ARMORY CASTLE, said to have used the flaw as a zero-day from early September 2026. CISA added it to the KEV catalog on November 20, with a November 23 federal patch deadline.
items.action: Patch vCenter to 9.1.1.0200, 9.0.2.0200, 8.0 U3m or 5.2.5 and hunt for rogue administrator accounts created before patching.

items.title: 1Password discloses breach via employee GitHub account; vaults unaffected
items.summary: 1Password disclosed on November 25 that an attacker accessed an employee's corporate GitHub account, introduced malicious code into server-side components and obtained some customer account data; passwords, vault contents and vault encryption keys were not affected.
items.details: Reported exposed data includes names and sign-in emails, account identifiers and timestamps, public keys and SRP parameters, and some invitation, provisioning and recovery tokens, plus private source code and CI/CD access. 1Password began investigating suspicious GitHub access on November 19. The number of affected customers has not been disclosed.
items.action: For 1Password business accounts, review admin activity, rotate provisioning and recovery tokens where advised by 1Password, and enforce phishing-resistant MFA on linked GitHub accounts.

items.title: Standard Chartered's Zodia Custody breached; client and employee contacts exposed
items.summary: Standard Chartered's crypto custody unit Zodia Custody confirmed a breach on November 26 that exposed business contact names and email addresses for a small number of clients and employees; no private keys were exposed and Zodia found no unauthorised transactions.
items.details: CEO Richard Clark told Reuters Zodia detected probing of its platform on Monday November 23 and temporarily shut down its business-to-business API. By November 24 it had determined an unauthorised party accessed publicly available details about client organisations alongside the contact data.
items.action: Zodia clients should treat inbound contact as higher phishing risk, verify any custody instruction change out of band, and confirm API reconnection steps directly with Zodia.

items.title: Inception ransomware claims Restaurant Brands International data (unverified claim)
items.summary: The Inception ransomware group claimed on November 26 to have data from Restaurant Brands International, including a claimed 126,038 unique Burger King US customers said to be extracted from the BK Guest Support Tool; the claim has not been independently verified and RBI had not confirmed it in the reporting.
items.details: The leak-site claim also alleges 216,156 ServiceNow incident folders from RBI Guest Care, employee OneDrive data and corporate Slack exports, with a stated deadline of November 27. Treat figures as attacker claims only, sourced from the group's listing as tracked on November 26.
items.action: No action for customers beyond phishing awareness; organisations using similar guest-care and ServiceNow setups should review GraphQL API access and attachment handling.

items.title: CERT-In flags critical flaws in Asus Armoury Crate and Control Center (CIVN-2026-0575)
items.summary: CERT-In issued a critical advisory on November 26 for Asus Armoury Crate and Control Center software, warning flaws could let a remote attacker bypass authentication, forge authentication tokens and gain elevated privileges.
items.details: Affected: Control Center Express before v1.7.29, Control Center Datacenter 4.0.0.2 and earlier, Control Center Enterprise 3.1.0.8 and earlier, and Armoury Crate up to and including v6.7.2. CERT-In attributes the flaws to hard-coded cryptographic keys, incorrect and missing authorisation checks and an untrusted search path, tracked as CVE-2026-114202, CVE-2026-114204, CVE-2026-114205, CVE-2026-126574 and CVE-2026-112115.
items.action: Install Asus's published security updates for Armoury Crate and Control Center across managed fleets and verify versions afterwards.

items.title: CERT-In issues high-severity warning for WhatsApp on Android, iOS, Mac and Windows
items.summary: CERT-In issued a high-severity advisory on November 26 flagging multiple flaws in WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business that could let attackers access sensitive information, run malicious code and bypass security restrictions.
items.details: Affected versions include WhatsApp for Android before 2.26.35.74 and 2.26.17.4, iOS before 2.26.24.72 and 2.26.15.72, Mac Desktop before 2.26.23.72 and Windows before 2.3000.1032164386.258709. CERT-In cited attachment spoofing, SQL injection, improper certificate chain validation and incomplete validation of AI-rich responses and external ad-reply URLs. The alert follows a recent MHA advisory on WhatsApp Web risks.
items.action: Update WhatsApp and WhatsApp Business to the latest releases on all platforms and push the update through MDM where managed.

items.title: Pixelleaks claims India's National Knowledge Network, Delhi PoP (unverified claim)
items.summary: The Pixelleaks ransomware group claimed on November 24 to have attacked NKN Delhi PoP (National Knowledge Network / NIC / MeitY), threatening to publish sensitive business records; the claim is from the group's leak site and has not been confirmed by NKN or NIC.
items.details: The group's statement describes the material as financial and operational business records from India's national research-network infrastructure and says representative records were examined by the group. No confirmation or scope statement from the affected organisation appeared in the reporting.
items.action: Treat as an unverified claim for monitoring; research and education networks connected via NKN should watch for related phishing and confirm any incident news only from NIC or MeitY statements.
